heading.purpose: Heading text, hierarchy level, optional numbering.

writer_guidance.level: 1 for the lesson title, 2 for a section, 3 for a subsection. Never skip a level.
writer_guidance.text: Name the content, not the pedagogy. No trailing punctuation.
writer_guidance.number: Only when the document numbers sections. Null otherwise — never invent numbering.

negative_cases: level 3 directly under level 1
heading as the final block of a section
heading text restating the sentence that follows it
heading.fragmentation: Must be bound with the first following block in one break-inside:avoid wrapper. Never render alone.
heading.emphasis: Type size, weight, rule, and spacing only. No box.

writer_guidance.paragraphs: One idea per paragraph, in reading order. Each paragraph is an array of inline nodes; use a term node for a defined term and a math node for notation. Do not emit an empty paragraph to create spacing.

negative_cases: a single-sentence paragraph that belongs in the previous paragraph
paragraphs used as disguised list items
an empty paragraph emitted for vertical spacing
prose.fragmentation: Splits freely with widows/orphans. Paragraphs may split.
prose.emphasis: Inline weight, italic, small caps, and whitespace. No background or border.

list.purpose: Ordered or unordered items with optional lead-in.

writer_guidance.style: ordered or steps when position carries meaning, unordered when it does not, glossary for term/definition pairs.
writer_guidance.lead_in: One clause naming what the items have in common. Null when the preceding prose already says it.
writer_guidance.items: Parallel grammatical form across every item. Keep each item within wordsPerItem; an item needing a sentence of explanation belongs in prose.

negative_cases: two items
items of mixed grammatical form
an item whose text is a full explanatory paragraph
style: ordered where order is arbitrary
list.fragmentation: List may split between items; individual item avoids splitting when practical.
list.emphasis: Markers, hanging indent, weight, and spacing. No box.

table.purpose: Columns, rows, header, caption, and semantic presentation hint.

writer_guidance.columns: First column is the row label. Every other column header names one criterion applied identically down the column.
writer_guidance.rows: Cell values keyed by column id. Every cell must be fillable with a comparable value — never 'n/a'.
writer_guidance.caption: States what the reader should notice. Null when the surrounding prose already does.
writer_guidance.presentation: comparison when the columns are the things compared, timeline when the first column is time, standard otherwise.

negative_cases: a single value column
a cell containing a full sentence
an empty or 'n/a' cell
row keys that do not match declared column ids
table.fragmentation: May split across pages. thead repeats. Rows avoid splitting.
table.emphasis: Rules, alignment, weight, and sparse header tint only when photocopy-safe. No enclosing box.

figure.purpose: Image or SVG asset, caption, alt text, width hint.

writer_guidance.asset: Reference an existing asset by identity. Never invent a path or describe an image that has not been produced.
writer_guidance.caption: Say what the reader should take from the figure, not what it depicts. Null when the prose already says it.
writer_guidance.alt_text: Describe the information the figure carries for a reader who cannot see it. Required even when a caption exists.
writer_guidance.width: span only when detail is lost at main-column width.

negative_cases: asset reference that does not resolve
alt_text repeating the caption verbatim
decorative image with no informational content
caption restating the preceding paragraph
figure.fragmentation: Figure and caption are atomic. May move to next page.
figure.emphasis: Scale, whitespace, caption typography, and optional hairline around the plate only—not a card.

aside.purpose: Short set-apart note with optional student-facing label.

writer_guidance.label: A short student-facing cue such as the teacher label for the intent. Null when the body speaks for itself.
writer_guidance.body: One point, self-contained, readable out of sequence. Stay inside bodyMaxWords — an aside that overflows is prose.

negative_cases: body longer than bodyMaxWords
more than maxPerSection asides in one section
content the reader must read in order to follow the main flow
label longer than labelMaxWords
aside.fragmentation: Atomic. Margin placement uses float, clear:right, and negative margin. Move cleanly if it does not fit.
aside.emphasis: The only object allowed a border or background. Default is a single vertical rule with restrained label.

worked-example.purpose: Problem/setup, ordered reasoning steps, final answer, optional checks.

writer_guidance.title: Names the method being demonstrated. Null when the problem statement is self-explanatory.
writer_guidance.problem: A concrete instance with every value the learner needs. Stay inside problemMaxWords.
writer_guidance.steps: Each step states what is done and why. No step may be left for the learner to supply — that is guided practice, not a demonstration.
writer_guidance.answer: The final result, stated plainly. Required; a worked example without an answer is rejected.
writer_guidance.check: How the reader verifies the answer is reasonable. Null when no cheap check exists.

negative_cases: missing answer
a step whose working is elided for the learner to complete
fewer than stepsMin steps
steps that state what is done without why
worked-example.fragmentation: May split between steps. A step avoids internal split where practical. Final step and answer stay together.
worked-example.emphasis: Numbered steps, hanging labels, indentation, and rules. No enclosing box.

questions.purpose: Open prompts, marks, response guidance, answer-space specification.

writer_guidance.items: One prompt per item, within stemMaxWords. Set answer space from the expected response length, and marks only where the document awards them. Expected answers belong in the teacher edition, never in the student prompt.
writer_guidance.instructions: How to respond, when it is not obvious. Null otherwise.

negative_cases: a prompt whose answer is a fixed choice from a closed set
an item with no question in it
expected answer text placed in the student-visible prompt
answer space too small for the expected response
questions.fragmentation: Split between questions, never inside a question. Prompt stays with minimum answer space.
questions.emphasis: Hanging numbers, marks aligned to edge, ruled answer space. No cards.

writer_guidance.stem: One question, answerable without reading the options first. Stay inside stemMaxWords.
writer_guidance.options: Between optionsMin and optionsMax options with stable ids and parallel form. Every wrong option must be one a real learner would pick, and for what reason. Correctness is carried in the teacher edition, not printed beside the option.
writer_guidance.marks: Only when the document awards marks. Null otherwise.

negative_cases: a filler distractor no learner would choose
'all of the above' or 'none of the above'
options of unequal length that signal the answer
the correct option marked in student-visible content
choices.fragmentation: Atomic when it fits; otherwise keep stem with at least two options and split only between options.
choices.emphasis: Letters A/B/C/D, hanging indent, whitespace. Never radio controls.

answer-key.purpose: Question references, expected answers, alternatives, working, rubric and misconceptions.

writer_guidance.groups: One group per source block, in document order. Each entry references the question it answers, gives the expected answer plus acceptable alternatives, and names the misconception a wrong answer reveals where the source block declared one. Never introduce an answer for a question that is not in the document.

negative_cases: an entry referencing a question id that is not in the document
answer-key content appearing in the student edition
an entry with no expected answer
alternatives that contradict the expected answer
answer-key.fragmentation: Split between entries. Entry keeps question reference with first answer line.
answer-key.emphasis: Heading hierarchy, compact typography, rules. No card.
